title: Curcumin Promotes Ferroptosis-Associated Responses and Increases the Antiproliferative Effect of Oxaliplatin in Oxaliplatin-Resistant Colorectal Cancer Cells
content: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and resistance to oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy continues to limit treatment efficacy. Ferroptosis has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for targeting therapy-resistant cancers. This study investigated whether curcumin promotes ferroptosis-associated responses and enhances the antiproliferative effect of oxaliplatin in an established oxaliplatin-resistant colorectal cancer cell model (HT29-OxaR). Cell viability was evaluated using the CCK-8 assay, while intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and lipid peroxidation were assessed by flow cytometry. Ferroptosis involvement was further examined using the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1. Curcumin reduced the viability of HT29-OxaR cells, increased intracellular ROS accumulation and lipid peroxidation, and the cytotoxic effect was partially attenuated by ferrostatin-1 pretreatment. These findings support the involvement of ferroptosis-associated mechanisms in the response of oxaliplatin-resistant colorectal cancer cells to curcumin. Although additional mechanistic studies are required to confirm the underlying molecular pathways, the present results support further investigation of curcumin as a potential adjunct therapeutic strategy for targeting ferroptosis-associated vulnerabilities in oxaliplatin-resistant colorectal cancer.
